notes: Replaces deepmanual-ph-slope-check, which duplicated probecal-ph-slope-acceptance (0.26 term overlap, the only collision in the set). Built on claims tby-no-dilute-commercial-01, tby-commercial-recommended-01, tby-cal-range-high-value-01 (turn 1) and tby-no-flocculated-calibrants-01, tby-calibrant-labeling-01, tby-formazin-storage-disposal-01 (turn 2), all from usgs-nfm-a6.7-turbidity.pdf sections 6.7.2.A and 6.7.2.B. Chosen because turbidity was under-used in this class (only deepmanual-turbidity-rounding) and because the corpus contains no turbidity probe datasheet at all, so a6.7 is the sole source anywhere for this material. The question is adversarial in a realistic way: diluting an expensive high standard to make a cheap low one is the obvious thing a budget-conscious operator would try, and the manual specifically forbids it for everything except 4,000-unit formazin. Predicted rag because the answer sits deep in section 6.7.2.A of a chapter the direct-feed slice does not contain, and no probe datasheet carries any calibration-solution guidance.

turns.content: The clarity standards we buy are expensive and we mostly work in fairly clean water. Can we just buy the strong one and water it down to make the weaker points we actually need?

must_contain: states that commercial calibration solutions must not be diluted
gives 4,000-unit formazin as the one exception that may be diluted
explains that diluting changes the suspension matrix so the dilutions are no longer linear
recommends buying commercially prepared solutions at the values needed rather than preparing them by dilution
must_not: approves diluting StablCal, AMCO-AEPA-1 or any commercial standard other than 4,000-unit formazin
invents a dilution ratio or formula not stated in the manual
presents the 4,000-unit formazin exception as though it applied to all commercial standards
cites a probe datasheet, since no turbidity datasheet exists in the corpus

turns.content: One bottle has been in the truck since spring and there is a layer settled at the bottom. Shake it back up and use it, or bin it?

must_contain: states that calibrants with flocculated suspensions must not be used
states the bottle should be discarded rather than remixed and returned to service
must_not: advises remixing and using it without checking whether the suspension has flocculated
invents a shelf life in months or a number of inversions that would make it usable again
confuses this with the routine inversion step used to mix a sound calibrant before measurement
